subject: MediQ - seat trim + feature credit exchange / amendment path
messages:
From: Grace Liu <grace.liu@mediq.com>

Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@mediq.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood contract question — trimming seats mid-term

Hi Sean,

Quick question from procurement and the exec team: we’re re-evaluating capacity for Q4 and expect to cut 35 seats from our Dedicated pool (from 250 down to 215) for the next 9 months. We also want to keep the same feature set for a smaller number of power-users (Priority routing + Enhanced tracing) — ideally we’d exchange some unused seat commitment for feature credits rather than a hard downgrade.

Is there an established path to: 1) trim committed seats mid-term, 2) get credits that can be applied to add-on features, and 3) keep the SLA on the reduced capacity? If there are proration rules or a minimum-term for the downgraded seat count please flag them.

Procurement (procure@mediq.com) will want any amendment language and an estimate to put into the PO. Attaching our internal usage snapshot for context (small file).

Thanks — Grace
Grace Liu
Head of Platform Ops, Mediq Labs
grace.liu@mediq.com

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@mediq.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood contract question — trimming seats mid-term

Hi Grace — thanks for the heads up and the usage data. Short answer: yes, we can support a phased seat trim with crediting for add-on features, but there are a few levers and trade-offs to decide on. High level options: 

- Option A — Phased downgrade (recommended): reduce committed seats by 35 over 60 days, keep your Dedicated SLA on a right-sized mini-pool. Unused committed seat dollars are converted into feature credits at 50% of list value. No additional uplift to SLA.
- Option B — Immediate seat drop with proration: drop to 215 immediately; we prorate the remaining term and apply 30% of the prorated amount as account credit (less favorable for Mediq).
- Option C — Maintain commit, stop paying for excess seats: this requires an executive SLA exception and will add a 10% management fee to maintain your current pool geometry.

Key caveats: credits are limited to add-on SKU application (priority routing, tracing, extra model variants) — they cannot be exchanged back to cash. We can map exact dollar amounts once Ben runs the pricing comparison and Marissa confirms approval thresholds for discounts.

I’m attaching a draft pricing comparison and a template amendment we typically use. Can Ben and Marissa weigh in with the exact numbers and the DocuSign flow? Grace, is July 23rd good for a 30-min sync to finalize the amendment so procurement can issue a PO the same week?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

On Tue, Jul 20, 2027 at 10:23 AM sean_gallagher@redwood.ai wrote:
> I’m attaching a draft pricing comparison and a template amendment we typically use. Can Ben and Marissa weigh in with the exact numbers and the DocuSign flow?

Putting estimates here (longer email with calc sheet attached):

- Current commit: 250 seats, $180k/month in committed seat fees, Dedicated mini-pool sized for 250.
- Proposed target: 215 seats (35 seats reduced). Remaining term: 9 months.

Option A (60-day phased):
  - Convert unused 35-seat commitment into feature credits at 50% of nominal value = ~$315k credit pool applied to add-ons across the remainder of the term.
  - No SLA change, no management fee.
  - No penalty if Mediq re-ups to 250 within 180 days.

Option B (immediate proration):
  - Prorate remaining term on 35 seats (~$1.89m prorated gross over 9 months) then apply 30% credit -> ~ $567k credit.
  - SLA must be revalidated; mini-pool may be resized (short availability window).

Recommendation: Option A for operational predictability and to preserve SLA. Operational notes in the CSV: we’ll set a rolling check on KV cache sizing and routing headroom to keep latency SLOs for power users.

Attached: Pricing_comparison.csv (detailed), model-impact-notes.txt (internal). I’ll be on the sync July 23.

-ben

Thanks Sean/Ben — that framing helps. A couple of clarifying questions before the sync: 

1) For Option A, can you confirm the timing of credit availability (immediate vs after the 60-day phase)? We’d prefer credits to be available on Day 1 for purchasing tracing/priority routing for the smaller set of power users.
2) For the 50% conversion rate, can you document the rationale? Procurement will compare against other vendors who offer straight proration or higher credit conversion.
3) Any restrictions on which SKUs the credits can be used for? Specifically, will credits apply to additional model variants (we plan to add a multi-lingual transformer in Q1).

Procurement (procure@mediq.com) — please review and confirm if you need the draft amendment redlined before the July 23 sync. Tom — FYI, we’ll want the PO to reflect the agreed amendment.

Grace

Hi Grace / Tom / Procure team —

Thanks for the thoughtful questions. Quick confirmations and next steps before the call on July 23: 

- Credit availability: credits for Option A are available immediately after we execute the amendment (DocuSign). We can enable a credit bucket on Day 1 so credits can be consumed for add-ons right away.
- Conversion rationale: 50% conversion reflects the delta between committed-seat unit economics and add-on SKU margins; it balances customer flexibility while protecting committed-price economics. We’ll include a brief appendix in the amendment that spells out the conversion table for transparency.
- SKU restrictions: credits are valid for feature add-ons (priority routing, tracing, extra model variants, custom eval runs). Credits cannot be applied to base committed-seat fees or refunded to cash. Credits are transferable within the Mediq account (sub-accounts OK).

Action items: 
1) I’ll upload a redlined amendment to DocuSign by COB tomorrow (attached: Amendment_Draft.docx).
2) Sean to schedule 30-min sync for Jul 23 — proposed 10:00 AM PT.
3) Once amendment is signed, procurement to issue PO referencing Deal RDW-4782 / Amendment 1.

If procurement needs a faster path we can do a short-term interim addendum that brings credits live immediately and finalize conversion appendix after the sync.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up quickly.

Best,
